items.title: foldable aluminum beach wagon integrates electric propulsion for soft-sand mobility
items.summary_original: LITEFAR B1 Wagon reimagines the journey from car to shore LITEFAR B1 is a foldable electric beach wagon designed to transport chairs, coolers, towels, and other equipment from vehicles to the shoreline across pavement, wooden paths, grass, and soft sand. The design integrates the frame, wheels, power system, and controls into a single structure, combining an aluminum -alloy frame with internally routed wiring, dual hub motors, and wide balloon tires. The B1 is organized around a series of vertical columns that define the frame, folding mechanism, and electrical system. Motor and control wiring is routed inside the structure, keeping the exterior free of exposed cables and separate technical components. B1 combines storage, mobility, and shade within a compact beach setup | all images ©LITE
items.title_de: Der faltbare Strandwagen aus Aluminium verfügt über einen Elektroantrieb für Mobilität auf weichem Sand
items.summary_de: Der LITEFAR B1 Wagon stellt die Reise vom Auto zum Strand neu dar. LITEFAR B1 ist ein faltbarer elektrischer Strandwagen, der für den Transport von Stühlen, Kühlboxen, Handtüchern und anderer Ausrüstung von Fahrzeugen zum Strand über Gehwege, Holzwege, Gras und weichen Sand entwickelt wurde. Das Design integriert Rahmen, Räder, Antriebssystem und Bedienelemente in einer einzigen Struktur und kombiniert einen Rahmen aus Aluminiumlegierung mit innen verlegter Verkabelung, Doppelnabenmotoren und breiten Ballonreifen. Der B1 ist um eine Reihe vertikaler Säulen herum organisiert, die den Rahmen, den Klappmechanismus und das elektrische System definieren. Motor- und Steuerkabel werden innerhalb der Struktur verlegt, so dass die Außenseite frei von freiliegenden Kabeln und separaten technischen Komponenten bleibt. items.title: modularized open steel grid reshapes family living on tight site in taiwan
items.summary_original: MOM House Replaces Concrete House with Expandable Steel Grid Located at the end of a narrow dead-end alley in Kaohsiung, Taiwan , MOM House by Supra-Simplicities + KCCS replaces an aging two-story reinforced concrete dwelling with a lightweight steel residence for a retired mother and flexible accommodation for her two adult children. The site is enclosed on three sides by neighboring houses and a school, with a single point of access and limited daylight and natural ventilation. Its adjacency to the school's sports field, however, provides an open outlook that becomes a key spatial and environmental element of the design. To minimize the family's displacement during construction, the project uses a prefabricated steel construction system that allows for rapid assembly and reoccupation. Na
items.title_de: Modularisiertes, offenes Stahlgitter gestaltet das Familienleben auf engem Raum in Taiwan neu
items.summary_de: MOM House ersetzt Betonhaus durch erweiterbares Stahlgitter. Das MOM House von Supra-Simplicities + KCCS befindet sich am Ende einer engen Sackgasse in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, und ersetzt ein in die Jahre gekommenes zweistöckiges Stahlbetonhaus durch ein leichtes Stahlhaus für eine Mutter im Ruhestand und eine flexible Unterkunft für ihre beiden erwachsenen Kinder. Das Gelände ist auf drei Seiten von benachbarten Häusern und einer Schule umschlossen, mit einem einzigen Zugangspunkt und begrenztem Tageslicht und natürlicher Belüftung. Die Nähe zum Sportplatz der Schule bietet jedoch einen offenen Ausblick, der zu einem zentralen räumlichen und ökologischen Element des Entwurfs wird. Um die Vertreibung der Familie während des Baus zu minimieren, verwendet das Projekt ein vorgefertigtes Stahlbausystem, das eine schnelle Montage und Wiederbelegung ermöglicht. N / A

items.title: 405 days from sketch to supercar, audi nuvolari arrives in monterey
items.summary_original: audi nuvolari arrives on the quail lawn At The Quail during Monterey Car Week , designboom was there as Audi unveiled the Nuvolari to the crowd, bringing its new hybrid supercar onto a lawn crowded with historic racers and rare collector cars. First revealed in Antibes in June (see designboom's coverage here ), the near-production prototype is limited to 499 examples, with European orders opening later this year and first deliveries planned for the first half of 2027. In person, its low mid-engine body reads as unusually direct for a car carrying this much hardware, a broad Titanium-colored volume pulled tight around the wheels and broken by deep channels for air. The number that keeps following the Nuvolari is 405. That is how many days passed between the first sketch and a drivable proto

items.summary_original: With gestures and postures doing the heavy lifting, the artist tells us why hands have become a recurring motif in her work. "I always wanted to be an artist," says Stefhany Lozano , and looking at her childhood, it's hard to imagine how she could have ended up doing anything else. Born in Bogotá, Colombia, 40 years ago, she grew up in a house where art books filled the shelves, where her aunt painted, where her grandmother loved to talk about art over dinner, and where Sunday mornings meant museum visits with her grandfather. Even so, her path wasn't a straight line. items.title: Stylenoir Script
items.summary_original: Stylenoir Script is a new display typeface from The Northern Block type foundry . Taking inspiration from hand-painted signage, brush lettering, and urban graffiti culture, its design reflects the ongoing evolution of lettering by combining traditional craftsmanship with the vibrant energy of street graffiti. The type family includes two styles: Smooth and Rough. Smooth offers a refined, polished look with clean lines while maintaining expressive movement and handwritten rhythm. Rough emphasises the raw quality of brush lettering through textured edges, subtle imperfections, and organic irregularities, recreating the appearance of lettering made with a dry brush or marker. Spacing, letter connections, and visual rhythm were carefully considered to ensure a strong visual impact. Contextual

items.title: who gets to live in the wall? architecture makes room for nonhuman residents
items.summary_original: architecture decides who gets in Architecture has always made decisions about who gets inside. Walls separate one environment from another, roofs close the gap overhead, and increasingly controlled building envelopes keep the human interior dry and predictable. Birds nesting beneath the eaves or insects finding their way into a cavity tend to enter the conversation later, usually as maintenance. Across a group of projects that designboom has followed over the past decade, architects are beginning with a different premise. Some openings stay open on purpose. At ChartierDalix’s School of Science and Biodiversity in Boulogne-Billancourt, France, completed in 2014, the concrete envelope was formed with ledges, hollows, cracks and crevices where vegetation and wildlife could establish themselve

items.summary_de: Architektur entscheidet darüber, wer reinkommt. Architektur hat schon immer Entscheidungen darüber getroffen, wer reinkommt. Wände trennen eine Umgebung von einer anderen, Dächer schließen die Lücke nach oben und zunehmend kontrollierte Gebäudehüllen halten den menschlichen Innenraum trocken und vorhersehbar. Vögel, die unter der Dachtraufe nisten, oder Insekten, die ihren Weg in einen Hohlraum finden, neigen dazu, später ins Gespräch zu kommen, meist als Unterhaltung. Bei einer Reihe von Projekten, die designboom im letzten Jahrzehnt verfolgt hat, gehen Architekten von einer anderen Prämisse aus. Einige Stellen bleiben absichtlich offen. An der 2014 fertiggestellten School of Science and Biodiversity von ChartierDalix in Boulogne-Billancourt, Frankreich, wurde die Betonhülle mit Vorsprüngen, Vertiefungen, Rissen und Spalten geformt, in denen sich Vegetation und Wildtiere etablieren konnten

items.title: How Baseline Can Help You Ship Less JavaScript
items.summary_original: Most of us install a dependency once and never look at it again. It does its job, the tests pass, and we move on. But the web platform keeps moving too, and a surprising number of the libraries sitting in your package.json today are now built into the browser. In a typical mid-sized JavaScript app, you can often find somewhere between 60KB and 90KB (minified and gzipped) of dependencies that the platform can now handle on its own. Date and number formatting, HTTP requests, modals, tooltips, deep cloning, grouping arrays: these were all real gaps a few years ago. A lot of them aren’t gaps anymore. items.title: What Star Wars got wrong about AI (so far)
items.summary_original: Two generations learned what a thinking machine looks like from a production line of individuals and the picture is not holding. AI assisted. The saga imagined thinking machines as immortal individuals in metal bodies. Real AI showed up as copyable software, and every difference is worth understanding. We grew up with the droids. R2-D2 beeping through a firefight, C-3PO fretting about the odds of survival, a whole galaxy quietly run by machines that think. Many of the androids from Star Wars are the most likable robots in film, and they are also the wrong picture of artificial intelligence. That matters more than it should, because for two generations the droids were most people’s first and clearest mental model of a thinking machine and mental models, once they take hold, change is hard.
items.title_de: Was Star Wars in Bezug auf KI falsch gemacht hat (bisher)
items.summary_de: Zwei Generationen haben aus einer Produktionslinie von Individuen gelernt, wie eine Denkmaschine aussieht, und das Bild ist nicht haltbar. KI unterstützt. Die Saga stellte sich denkende Maschinen als unsterbliche Individuen in Metallkörpern vor. Echte KI zeigte sich als kopierbare Software, und jeder Unterschied ist verständlich. Wir sind mit den Droiden aufgewachsen. R2-D2 piepst während eines Feuergefechts, C-3PO macht sich Sorgen um seine Überlebenschancen, eine ganze Galaxie wird stillschweigend von denkenden Maschinen regiert. Viele der Androiden aus Star Wars sind die sympathischsten Roboter im Film, und sie vermitteln auch das falsche Bild von künstlicher Intelligenz. items.title: Constrictor
items.summary_original: Constrictor , a new type family released by Frere-Jones Type in June 2026, began as a title sketch for a documentary about Margaret Lovatt, who was part of a NASA funded project which set out to communicate with dolphins and ended up dosing them with LSD. Shallcrass layered this rich input with typographic history, experiences and memories from the physical world to create a variable font family which radiates an energetic presence and has movement at its core. According to Shallcrass, "Danger, tension and anxiety are key aspects of why the face works to me." Constrictor's variable width axis impacts our perception of noise when read: expand the letters and you can feel the rhythm ease; compress them and the letterforms begin to grip each other like a boa constrictor finding its hold. The more we trust a name, the less we question the machine wearing it, and the more that name has to lose when the machine is confidently wrong. A few weeks ago my team spent an hour arguing about whether to lie to people. We were designing the onboarding for an AI product, the first time user experience that tries to prove the product is worth their time. The fairly insignificant thing we were fighting about was whether to add a little animation that made it look like the software was thinking hard, adding a few seconds to the flow when really it could have been instantaneous. items.title_de: Wir verschlingen uns mit geliehenem Vertrauen und das wird uns teuer zu stehen kommen.
items.summary_de: Das vertrauenswürdige Gesicht ist die Maske, aber die Maschine darunter weiß nicht, wann es falsch ist, und genau das werden Sie nicht überprüfen. Je mehr wir einem Namen vertrauen, desto weniger stellen wir die Maschine in Frage, die ihn trägt, und desto mehr muss dieser Name verlieren, wenn die Maschine selbstbewusst falsch liegt. Vor ein paar Wochen hat mein Team eine Stunde lang darüber gestritten, ob man die Leute anlügen soll. Wir haben das Onboarding für ein KI-Produkt entworfen, das erste Benutzererlebnis, das beweisen soll, dass das Produkt seine Zeit wert ist. Die ziemlich unbedeutende Sache, über die wir gestritten haben, war, ob wir eine kleine Animation hinzufügen sollten, die den Anschein erweckte, als würde die Software angestrengt nachdenken, und so den Ablauf um ein paar Sekunden verlängern, obwohl er eigentlich augenblicklich hätte erfolgen können. Ein rasanter „Analysiere deine Antworten…“-Moment, in dem wir etwas Sprache und BH einbringen konnten

items.title: ‘nature becomes the choreographer’: janet echelman on a sky full of hope in frankfurt
items.summary_original: a sky full of hope moves above frankfurt Janet Echelman has spent much of her career persuading cities to look up. Her newest public artwork hangs over Konstablerwache, a broad central square in Frankfurt where commuters pass through and a market takes over twice a week. A Sky Full of Hope – Earthtime 1.78 Frankfurt stretches a field of colored fiber more than seven meters overhead, moving with the wind through the day and illumination after dark. More than 3,000 people gathered beneath it for its August 11th unveiling, filling the square and occupying nearly every deck chair by the afternoon.
